title: pr_scope 2.1.0 — sub-file dependency-direction scope check
intent: Close the gap that let PR #296 pass review: pr_scope compared divergence at FILE granularity, so a legitimately-declared package.json could carry an UNDECLARED dependency version change (a silent zod ^4.4.3 -> ^3.25.76 downgrade reverting PR #293). Add a per-dependency rule that looks INSIDE a declared package.json — declared file != declared change.

scope.out_of_scope_notes: Additive to pr_scope only. No new analyzer, no AnalyzerType enum change (reuses PR_SCOPE), no logic/golden/confidence manifest regen (AST hashes for those were re-verified green). Does not touch the ReviewContext no-injection guarantee — the new check reads the real git surface via `git show <ref>:<path>` and reuses the already-resolved merge_base.

what_changed: Added module helpers: _is_package_json, _parse_version (strips v^~>=<, rejects ranges), _version_direction (downgrade/upgrade/same/unknown), _read_package_deps (git show <ref>:<path>, status ok/absent/malformed/git_error).

Added rule pr_scope.undeclared_dependency_change: for each dependency changed inside a DECLARED package.json but NOT declared in scope.dependency_changes / diff_articulation, emit HIGH on a downgrade or a revert-of-base-landing, MEDIUM otherwise; metadata carries dependency, base_version, head_version, direction, reverts_base_landing.

Every failure mode is a Finding, never a raised exception: malformed package.json -> pr_scope.dependency_check_uncheckable (CRITICAL); any internal exception -> pr_scope.dependency_check_error (CRITICAL). An escaping exception would abort the scan — the silent pass this check exists to prevent.

Enumerated the new rule + severity policy in cbsp21/pr_scope_acceptance.json and added 8 tests reconstructing the #296 shape (HIGH downgrade fires; declared supabase-only stays silent; declared zod stays silent; undeclared upgrade = MEDIUM; undeclared package.json not double-reported; malformed = CRITICAL uncheckable; revert-of-base flag set; contract-valid findings).
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: Extends the existing pr_scope analyzer rather than adding a sibling. The file-level rule pr_scope.undeclared_file cannot see a change INSIDE a declared file; this is the strictly-additive sub-file granularity that #296 proved was missing.

commands_run: py -3.11 -m pytest tests/ -k "logic_manifest or golden or confidence_policy or signal_logic" -q
test_results: logic/golden/confidence/signal manifest tests: all passed — no AST-hash drift from the pr_scope.py edit.
verification.notes: Read-only against the real git surface; no synthetic-diff injection. Existing pr_scope behavior unchanged.
